issue_payload.body:
I needed a way to hide containers but I couldn't figure out a way to do so. 

I plan to update the docs and add an example, but could you check if you like the way it was programmed before I do that. 

Thanks a lot! 

Example usage
```
buildingContainer := widget.NewContainer(
		// the container will use a plain color as its background
		widget.ContainerOpts.BackgroundImage(image.NewNineSliceColor(color.NRGBA{0x13, 0x1a, 0x22, 0xff})),

		// the container will use an anchor layout to layout its single child widget
		widget.ContainerOpts.Layout(widget.NewRowLayout(
			widget.RowLayoutOpts.Spacing(10),
			widget.RowLayoutOpts.Padding(widget.Insets{
				Top:    10,
				Bottom: 10,
				Left:   10,
				Right:  10,
			}),
		)),
	)
buildingContainer.Hidden = true
```

So I've been playing around a bit and I think there's a corner case I'd like your thoughts on: Do hidden elements take up space? cc @mcarpenter622 

Here the Row Layout takes up space, but the buttons do not.  
![Taking up space](https://www.sava.be/images/ebitenui/hidden_take_up_space.gif)

Here the Row Layout doesn't take up space (buttons stay the same). 
![Not taking up space](https://www.sava.be/images/ebitenui/hidden_dont_up_space.gif)

In my case I want the row to take up space as it stops the row below from jumping up and down, but I don't want the buttons to do so. 

It kinda makes sense to not have Hidden options take up space, which would mean I need to work around the jumping up and down in my project, which I think I can do with an empty container.

issue_payload.body:
This was causing issues due to 'not visible buttons' being able to still be clicked.

To test the bug you can apply 

```diff
diff --git a/_examples/widget_demos/imagebutton/main.go b/_examples/widget_demos/imagebutton/main.go
index ea002b2..8767a44 100644
--- a/_examples/widget_demos/imagebutton/main.go
+++ b/_examples/widget_demos/imagebutton/main.go
@@ -64,6 +64,7 @@ func main() {
                        btnIconG.GetWidget().Disabled = !btnIconG.GetWidget().Disabled
                }),
        )
+       button.GetWidget().Visibility = widget.Visibility_Hide
        buttonStackedLayout.AddChild(button)
        // Put an image on top of the button, it will be centered.
        // If your image doesn't fit the button and there is no Y stretching support,
```
        
And then run ` go run ./_examples/widget_demos/imagebutton/`, then just click the circle and you'll see the log of `button clicked` which it should not.
        
This specific one can also be solved by :
        
```diff
        diff --git a/widget/stackedlayout.go b/widget/stackedlayout.go
index 456682b..3170a78 100644
--- a/widget/stackedlayout.go
+++ b/widget/stackedlayout.go
@@ -79,6 +79,9 @@ func (a *StackedLayout) Layout(widgets []PreferredSizeLocateableWidget, rect ima
        }
        rect = a.padding.Apply(rect)
        for idx := range widgets {
+               if !widgets[idx].GetWidget().IsVisible() {
+                       continue
+               }
                widgets[idx].SetLocation(rect)
        }
 }
```

IDK exaclty which is the best solution, but the StackedLayout one, even if this fixes the issue on the example, on my game still fails until I do it on the Widget.

On my game I have a modal with buttons and when one is clicked I hide  the content and display another content on top of it, but then if I clicked on that new content it would still trigger the hidden buttons.

So if it's fixed on the widget it cannot `fireEvents` which is at the end what is triggering the Click.
